feedbackItems.feedback: Three of the robots did a good job of getting parts and getting them to the machine. They had good collaberation. The poor blue robot looks lost with his part since the machine is full. He's not driving towards to be ready to load as soon as its ready.
The red robot did a good job of getting the box to the drop zone in the shortest path possible. It was an efficient route.
feedbackItems.reason: Some other robots did a less efficient route getting to the loading zone before, so the good route of the red robot caught my eye as a good thing.
I saw this as good efficient team work between the robots that should be noted.
feedbackItems.feedback: Good collaberation between the red and yellow robot getting the parts to one area and handing it over to the yellow robot.

feedbackItems.reason: The robot planned ahead and put the box out, so it would be ready to load the parts into out of the machine.
feedbackItems.feedback: Good job on the red robot part to get the box ready next to the machine, so it was ready for the next order. It staged the necessary item in the process. Great efficient teamwork!

surveyAnswers.q1: I mostly watched for behavior that I thought was either efficient or inefficient towards helping to manufacture and ship the item. Any unnecessary movements or lack of coordination caught my eye. Also when the robots worked together it was noticable and more efficient.
surveyAnswers.q4: This is a very interesting experiment. I have not done one like this before. It made me think critically about the manufacturing goals and how to best achieve that goal with the robots.
surveyAnswers.q2: It wasn't too hard, but the episodes with four robots did present a little bit harder challenge simply because there were more robots to watch. I tried to monitor them fairly equally ot make sure I did not miss anything important.
surveyAnswers.q3: Take 10-15 seconds to watch each robot exclusively vs trying to watch them all at once the whole time.
